hypotheses.justification: Follows from hn and hmn: if m = 0 then 0 ∣ n forces n = 0, contradicting 1 ≤ n. In the proof, replace the `hm_pos` line with a derivation from hn and hmn (e.g. `Nat.pos_of_ne_zero (by rintro rfl; simp_all)`); the rest is unchanged. Note: hm and hn cannot both be deleted (m = n = 0 makes the statement false: 0 = 1).

With hm kept, the only excluded case is n = 0. There `Nat.divisorsAntidiagonal_zero : divisorsAntidiagonal 0 = ∅` makes the left-hand sum 0, and the right-hand side `if 0 = m then 1 else 0` is 0 because m ≥ 1. Proof: case split on n = 0, close that case by simp, otherwise run the existing proof. (It can be deleted on its own, but not together with hm.)

If ¬ m ∣ n, the filtered set is empty: an x in n.divisorsAntidiagonal has x.1 * x.2 = n (Nat.mem_divisorsAntidiagonal), so m ∣ x.2 would give m ∣ n. The sum is therefore 0. The right-hand side is also 0, since n = m would give m ∣ n via m ∣ m. Proof: `by_cases hmn : m ∣ n`; the positive case is the existing proof; the negative case uses Finset.sum_eq_zero (or filter_false_of_mem) on the left and if_neg on the right.
